lead.title: Gustave Roussy spin-off Orakl Oncology raises a $34M Series A to predict cancer drug responses with organoids and AI
lead.deck: The oversubscribed round (€31M) is co-led by Norrsken VC and Singular, with InfraVia, Serena, Bpifrance's Patient Autonome fund, teampact.ventures and Plug and Play; the Paris company, founded in 2023, has now raised $50M in total. It tests drugs on patient-derived tumour organoids and combines the results with clinical and molecular data (SCOPE v2 model, O-Predict offering); the money will increase data generation fivefold, add lung and gastric cancers and set up teams in the US and UK. Note: the claimed accuracy still rests on a non-peer-reviewed, mostly retrospective preprint.

milestone.title: Commit Biologics nominates COM002, the first candidate from its complement-recruiting antibody platform
milestone.summary: COM002 is a bispecific "immune engager" from the BiCE platform: instead of mobilising T cells, it triggers the complement system to destroy targeted cells. In non-human primates it produced targeted B-cell depletion; it will first target relapsed or refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma, then autoimmune diseases. The company also named Anne-Marie Levy Rasmussen COO and Benjamin Ole Wolthers Head of Clinical Development.
milestone.why: It marks the shift from platform to product for a Danish biotech backed by Novo Holdings, Bioqube Ventures, Korys and the BioInnovation Institute: an alternative to T-cell engagers, whose toxicity (cytokine release syndrome) limits their use in autoimmunity, and a milestone that usually precedes a financing round to reach the clinic.

deal.thesis: RTW Investments leads the round with GV, Janus Henderson, Ikarian Capital, Affinity Asset Advisors and Dellora, alongside Perceptive and Acorn Bioventures, to take NTX-253, an oral positive allosteric modulator (PAM) of the muscarinic M4 receptor, into Phase 2 in schizophrenia. After Cobenfy's success, the bet is to amplify natural acetylcholine rather than activate the receptor, for better tolerability; the arrival of Karuna veterans (Andrew Miller as executive chair) strengthens the thesis, but clinical efficacy remains to be shown.

brefsEurope.title: Helmholtz Munich spin-off Viacure secures a nearly €10M project for its anti-Inceptor antibody in type 2 diabetes
brefsEurope.summary: 80% funded by Saxony and the ERDF, with Fraunhofer IZI in Leipzig and CUP Laboratorien: the antibody blocks Inceptor, a receptor discovered in 2021 by Heiko Lickert's team, to preserve beta cells; the goal is to complete preclinical work by end-2028 ahead of a first-in-human trial.

brefsEurope.title: Windward Bio prices its Nasdaq IPO at $17 a share, with $50M from Sanofi in a private placement
brefsEurope.summary: About 10.3 million shares, or $225M gross including Sanofi's placement; trading under the symbol WWB from November 13. The Basel biotech, founded in 2024, develops long-acting anti-TSLP antibodies licensed from China (WIN378, WIN027) in asthma, COPD and atopic dermatitis.

brefsEurope.title: Mironid strengthens its board and clinical team for the Phase 1 of LoAc in polycystic kidney disease
brefsEurope.summary: The Glasgow biotech names Omar Khwaja non-executive director, Lars Erwig Chief Medical Advisor and Kimberly Hoffman Head of Clinical Operations; LoAc, a first-in-class small molecule for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, is in Phase 1, with Roche Venture Fund, Sofinnova and BioGeneration Ventures among its backers.

brefsEurope.title: TolerogenixX publishes preclinical proof of concept for its tolerogenic MIC cells in lupus nephritis in Kidney International
brefsEurope.summary: In NZB/W F1 mice, the patient's own immune cells treated ex vivo with mitomycin C slowed kidney disease (proteinuria, creatinine, anti-DNA antibodies); the company, already running a Phase IIb in kidney transplantation, plans to extend the platform to lupus and multiple sclerosis.

brefsEurope.title: Hemogenyx treats the first patient in the second cohort of its HG-CT-1 CAR-T in acute myeloid leukaemia
brefsEurope.summary: The dose was doubled on the recommendation of the safety monitoring board, which saw no dose-limiting toxicities in the first three adults of this Phase I trial in refractory AML; a paediatric arm is also recruiting.

brefsEurope.title: Lakefront (formerly Galapagos) drops its TYK2 inhibitor GLPG3667 after failing to find a partner
brefsEurope.summary: After a borderline Phase 2 in dermatomyositis, a miss in lupus and the FDA approval of Priovant's Lisraya in August, the company refocuses on its T-cell engagers led by gamgertamig; it remains open to licensing the discontinued programme.

brefsIntl.title: Biolojic Design gets FDA clearance for BD200, the first conjugated "multibody" to enter the clinic
brefsIntl.summary: An antibody whose arms can each bind Trop2 or Nectin-4, carrying a topoisomerase inhibitor payload: it is designed to adapt to each tumour's antigen profile. A global Phase 1 is expected to start in the coming weeks — a comparable for European bispecific ADCs.

brefsIntl.title: Blackstone commits up to $1.5B to Pfizer to fund Phase 3 of its monthly GLP-1 berobenatide
brefsIntl.summary: Payments phased through 2028 for up to ten Phase 3 trials, in exchange for milestones tied to FDA approval and sales targets. A comparable: private equity now directly funds the clinical risk of an obesity asset.

word.definition: A molecule that binds a receptor at a different spot from its natural messenger and, without activating it on its own, amplifies the response when that messenger is present — like a volume knob rather than an on/off switch.

parts.label: Orthosteric site
parts.role: the main lock, where the natural messenger binds (acetylcholine, glutamate, GABA)

parts.label: Allosteric site
parts.role: the control dial: a separate pocket, less conserved from one receptor subtype to another

parts.label: Modulator (PAM)
parts.role: the tuner: it makes the receptor more sensitive or more effective in response to the natural messenger

how.t: The PAM settles into the allosteric site and stabilises a more responsive form of the receptor, without triggering a signal by itself.
When the natural messenger arrives, the response is stronger: the timing and location of the physiological signal are preserved, since nothing happens in its absence.
Once all allosteric sites are occupied, the effect stops increasing: this "ceiling effect" limits overdose risk, and the less conserved site makes it possible to target a single receptor subtype.

word.why: Benzodiazepines are the historic PAMs of the GABA-A receptor; the new generation aims for selectivity to avoid sedation and side effects. The success of Cobenfy (Karuna, acquired by BMS) has revived neuropsychiatry, and investors are funding PAMs for specific receptors: Neurosterix raises $105M for its M4 PAM, Draig has raised $205M for its AMPA PAM. Due-diligence watch point: structure-activity relationships are often "flat" and small chemical changes can flip the effect (a PAM turning into a NAM).

startups.name: Neurosterix
startups.use: Addex spin-off; NTX-253, an oral PAM of the muscarinic M4 receptor for schizophrenia, moves into Phase 2 after a $105M Series B led by RTW Investments (November 2026).

startups.name: Draig Therapeutics
startups.use: DT-101, an oral AMPA receptor PAM, in Phase 2 in major depressive disorder (results expected in 2027); $205M raised, including a $65M Series B led by Deep Track Capital in July 2026.

startups.name: Engrail Therapeutics
startups.use: ENX-102, a GABA-A receptor PAM selective for the α2/α3/α5 subunits (sparing α1, which drives sedation), in Phase 2 in generalised anxiety disorder.
